identification.bodyShape: Fusiform, moderately compressed schooling predator with a large mouth and a prominent, protruding jaw.
identificationTraits: Prominent jaw with sharp, compressed, shearing teeth.
Small scales and an almost straight lateral line.
A single black blotch at the base of each pectoral fin, with no matching spot on the gill cover.
Dorsal and anal fins nearly equal in size and shape.
identification.coloration: Blue-green to bluish-gray on the back, silvery on the sides and belly.
identification.adultAppearance: A silvery, blue-backed schooling fish with a large toothy jaw, a nearly straight lateral line, and a single dark blotch at the pectoral-fin base.

similarSpecies.name: Crevalle jack (Caranx hippos)
similarSpecies.distinction: Deep-bodied with a steep head profile, a prominent black spot on the gill cover in addition to one at the pectoral-fin base, and no obviously visible teeth at typical viewing distance - bluefish is more fusiform, carries only the pectoral-base spot, and has conspicuous sharp teeth.

similarSpecies.name: Spanish mackerel (Scomberomorus maculatus)
similarSpecies.distinction: Slender and elongate with yellow-to-olive oval spots scattered over the body and a lateral line that drops abruptly below the second dorsal fin - bluefish lacks body spotting and has a deeper-bodied, less streamlined profile.

identification.averageAdultLength: Not given as a single figure separate from maximum size in the sources reviewed; matures at age 2, roughly 15-20 in.
identification.commonAnglingSize: Informally cited in the 3-5 lb range by one state agency source; not otherwise resolved to a length figure.
identification.typicalWeight: See commonAnglingSize; a typical-weight figure distinct from that was not sourced.
identification.maximumDocumentedSize: Up to about 39 in and 31 lb per NOAA Fisheries; a Florida state-record fish weighed 22 lb 2 oz.

social.note: Explicitly schooling, typically among similarly sized individuals, with schools described as covering vast areas of open water.

feedingStrategy.note: A voracious pursuit predator; the well-documented 'blitz' is large schools attacking baitfish at the surface, churning the water. Sharp shearing teeth allow it to take large prey items; diet centers on locally abundant schooling fish (menhaden, silversides) and squid, with documented cannibalism on smaller bluefish.

dielTendency.note: Not resolved to a specific diel pattern in the sources reviewed.

behavior.seasonalActivity: Strongly migratory: north and inshore as water warms in spring/summer, concentrating Maine to Cape Hatteras in summer, then south and offshore in fall/winter toward the South Atlantic Bight, with a marked winter concentration off Florida's Atlantic coast.
behavior.thermalDrivenBehavior: Juveniles are reported to move into estuaries once water temperature rises above about 13-15C/55-59F. Agency sources describe bluefish generally as a warm-temperate species with a preference for warmer conditions, without a further numeric adult preference range found.
behavior.depthMovement: Pelagic throughout life: larvae in roughly the upper 15 m, concentrated just below the surface; pelagic juveniles remain surface-associated; adults range through open water and inshore/nearshore habitat rather than holding a fixed depth.
behavior.coverUse: Not associated with hard structure in the sources reviewed; juveniles use soft estuarine substrate and occasionally grass, algae or oyster beds, but the species is fundamentally a pelagic, bait-following predator rather than a structure fish.
behavior.predatorAvoidance: Not sourced beyond noting that bluefish are themselves prey for sharks (including shortfin mako), tunas, billfish, and seabirds (on juveniles).
behavior.spawningBehavior: Multiple spawning events in spring and summer in open ocean water, producing distinct spring-, summer- and fall-spawned cohorts; eggs are pelagic, hatching in about 2 days at 18-22C/64-72F. Spawning location and any staging concentration are excluded from targeting in this catalog.

diet.primaryNote: A voracious, sharp-toothed pursuit predator on schooling baitfish - principally menhaden and silversides - and squid, with documented cannibalism on smaller bluefish. This is diet capacity, not a current bait event; the well-known surface 'blitz' is feeding behavior, and this record does not predict its timing or location.

lifeStageDiet.youngOfYear: Copepods for the first 2-4 weeks post-hatch, shifting to piscivory by about 40 mm body length.
lifeStageDiet.adult: Locally abundant schooling fish and benthic invertebrates, with menhaden and silversides specifically documented, plus squid.

diet.preySizeShifts: Shift from copepod prey to piscivory occurs by about 40 mm body length; further size-class detail into adulthood was not sourced.
diet.ontogeneticShift: Zooplanktivory as very early juveniles, shifting rapidly to piscivory.
diet.observedForageRule: Diet capacity is not proof of a current bait event, including the surface blitz, which this record does not predict.

seasonal_calendar.overview: Bluefish is a pelagic, schooling migrant whose year is organized around latitude and temperature rather than a fixed structure. Juveniles use estuarine nursery water; adults are open-water pursuit predators on schooling baitfish, most visibly in the surface 'blitz'. This record covers inshore estuarine water only - open-ocean nearshore and surf-zone use is well known in general angling literature but was not sourced to agency material with enough holding-class specificity to include here this session.

entries.habitatClass: Inshore estuarine and coastal water as the population moves north.
entries.movementTendency: Northward migration as water warms; juveniles enter estuaries once temperature rises above about 55-59F.
entries.conservationNote: One of several spring/summer spawning events occurs in open ocean water during this window; conservation context only.
entries.presentationImplication: Run-and-gun cast and horizontal retrieve become viable as schools move into inshore water.
invalidators: treating spring as a fixed date rather than the sourced temperature threshold

entries.habitatClass: Estuarine and coastal water, concentrating Maine to Cape Hatteras.
entries.feedingEmphasis: Pursuit predation on schooling baitfish, including the surface blitz.
entries.presentationImplication: Run-and-gun cast into visible surface activity without running the school over; horizontal retrieve through the water column when fish are not surfaced.
invalidators: treating a surface blitz as a location to return to - this record gives no coordinates and none should be inferred
predicting when or where a blitz will occur

entries.habitatClass: Departing inshore water for the continental shelf and points south.
entries.movementTendency: Southward, offshore migration toward the South Atlantic Bight.
entries.presentationImplication: Inshore presentations lose fish progressively as the population moves offshore and south; this record does not extend guidance to the water types that migration passes through.
invalidators: reading a thinning fall bite as a location problem rather than the stock leaving the water type this record covers

entries.habitatClass: South Atlantic Bight and Florida's Atlantic coast, outside the water type reviewed in this record.
entries.conservationNote: Not covered by this record's inshore-only presentation guidance.
